title: Dial-a-Curse

scenario.title: Reproducible fake test data
scenario.body: Programs like this fill test databases with fake names and fake reviews. That needs promises: the same seed gives the same rows, asking for more rows doesn't change the first ones, and no row repeats (a column that must be unique would reject it). The book's version repeats itself about once every 30 lines, and asking for 40 adjectives when there are only 36 crashes it. Keep every seeded answer the author expects and make those promises too.

character.name: Sir Bluster
character.role: a hammy old actor who hurls Shakespeare's insults

tagline: Sir Bluster has been on the stage for 400 years and can't stop insulting people the way Shakespeare did: "You peevish, foolish gull!" Choose how many insults, how many fancy words in each, and a lucky number. Same lucky number, same insults.

brain_blurbs.book: Picks words at random, one insult after another.
brain_blurbs.real: Picks the same way, but never says the same insult twice and knows when it's run out of words.

rules.test_usage: Explains himself when you ask for help
rules.test_bad_adjective_str: "How many words?" needs a whole number, not letters
rules.test_bad_adjective_num: …and it has to be more than 0
rules.test_bad_number_str: "How many insults?" needs a whole number
rules.test_bad_number_int: …and it has to be more than 0
rules.test_bad_seed: The lucky number has to be a whole number
rules.test_01: Lucky number 1, one insult: exactly the book's insult
rules.test_02: Lucky number 2: exactly the book's three insults
rules.test_03: Lucky number 3, five insults with one word each: exactly the book's
rules.test_04: Lucky number 4, two insults with four words each: exactly the book's
rules.test_same_seed_same_insults: Same lucky number, same insults, every time
rules.test_more_insults_keep_the_first_ones: Asking for more insults doesn't change the first ones
rules.test_no_repeated_insults: 300 insults and not one said twice
rules.test_too_many_adjectives_is_polite: Asking for 40 fancy words (there are only 36) gets a polite no
rules.test_too_many_insults_is_polite: Asking for more insults than exist gets a polite no
rules.test_different_seeds_differ: Different lucky numbers give different insults
rules.test_every_insult_is_well_formed: Every insult is "You …, … noun!" made of real Shakespeare words
rules.test_never_repeats: Any lucky number, any amount: no insult twice
rules.test_longer_batch_starts_the_same: A long list always starts like the short one
rules.test_every_word_at_once: All 36 fancy words in one insult is fine
rules.test_every_possible_insult: Can say every one of the 1,404 one-word insults, each once
